chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Four [characteristics] in whomsoever they are found, God will spread His protection over him and admit him into Paradise within His mercy: good character by which he lives among people, gentleness with the afflicted, compassion for the parents, and kindness to the servant.'

key_terms.نَشَرَ اللَّهُ كَنَفَهُ: God spread His protection/wings over him

ai.seo_question: What are the four characteristics that ensure God's protection and entry into Paradise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith links moral excellence (*husn al-khuluq*) directly to divine protection (*kaf al-Rahman*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on character as a prerequisite for spiritual elevation. The inclusion of kindness to servants highlights the social justice dimension of faith, while the specific mention of parental compassion underscores the high status of *birr al-walidayn* in Shia ethics. This narration serves as a practical guide for integrating piety into daily social interactions, ensuring that religious observance extends beyond ritual to encompass interpersonal mercy.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-57 Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated that his father quoted his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Maymun , on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “

Whoever has four characteristics shall be protected by God and taken to Paradise: being good-tempered so as to live amongst the people; sympathizing with the ones who have suffered from calamities; being kind to their parents; and treating servants kindly.”
